findings.title: Dimensions guard confirmed to precede every consumer of Dimensions
findings.claim: The guard at marshal.go:992-1003 sits ahead of every consumer of Dimensions (both float fast paths, vectorSliceReuse, reflect.MakeSlice, the array check, elemSize = len(data)/Dimensions).

findings.title: vectorElemMinSize recursion confirmed to terminate and partition correctly
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize's recursion terminates structurally and partitions correctly against isVectorVariableLengthType.

findings.title: getCassandraLongType behaviour change confirmed safe, single gated consumer
findings.claim: getCassandraLongType's changed behaviour has one consumer (helpers.go:55,59), gated behind a prefix the earlier branch already intercepts.

findings.title: Overflow-saturation branch in vectorElemMinSize has zero test coverage
findings.claim: The `return math.MaxInt32` overflow-saturation branch shows 0 hits in the coverage profile while every other block in vectorElemMinSize is covered; it is wire-reachable (e.g. vector<vector<float,600000000>,N> via strconv.Atoi at helpers.go:264) and is the only new arithmetic in a PR about arithmetic going silently wrong that remains unpinned by a test.

findings.title: Nested-vector unknown-type error message omits element type and dimension
findings.claim: VectorType has no String(), so %v falls through to the promoted NativeType.String() and the error reads 'no Go type for element type custom(...VectorType)' with no element type or dimension; the commit's stated purpose is met for unknown basic types but not for the nested-vector case, and the same issue exists at marshal.go:1118.

findings.title: Negative dimensions on a NULL payload now errors instead of returning nil
findings.claim: Base code returned nil for negative dimensions on a NULL payload because the data==nil branch ran first; the new code now errors instead — deliberate, test-pinned, and arguably better, but a behaviour change absent from the description's list.

findings.title: Zero-dimension inner vector floored at 1 byte rejects a payload that used to decode fine
findings.claim: vector<vector<int,0>,3> over an empty payload decoded to [[] [] []] on base but now errors '3 dimensions do not fit in 0 bytes' because the minimum-size floor is 1 byte while the true wire size is 0; pathological and moot once dim<1 is rejected, but it's a third unlisted behaviour change, and the code comment explains the divide-by-zero mechanism without noting the bound is stricter than the wire format.

findings.title: vectorElemMinSize still nil-derefs on a nil SubType when Dimensions>0
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize nil-derefs on a nil SubType when Dimensions>0; not a regression (exact parity with the old fast path) and unreachable from the wire, but VectorType/SubType/Dimensions are exported and the guard's comment already reasons about caller-supplied nil subtypes yet stops short of covering zero dimensions.

findings.title: Allocation test asserts on process-global runtime.TotalAlloc
findings.claim: The allocation assertion reads process-global runtime.TotalAlloc; held under -count=5, -shuffle=on with 128KB headroom against ~3.5KB actual, but the 'not parallel' comment only covers sibling subtests, not the suite's background dialers/loggers — the margin carries it, not isolation.
